new_entities.name: Boron supplementation
new_entities.description: Supplemental boron taken orally with the aim of changing hormone or inflammatory markers.

new_entities.name: Free testosterone
new_entities.description: The unbound testosterone fraction available in circulation.

edges.effect_quant: A tiny 2011 human trial reported higher morning free testosterone after one week of 10 mg/day boron, but an older placebo-controlled bodybuilding study found no meaningful testosterone effect over seven weeks.
edges.population: healthy adult men, including recreationally trained bodybuilders and healthy volunteers
edges.mechanism: Boron may transiently shift steroid binding or metabolism rather than acting as a robust androgen stimulator. The short-term signal most often cited comes alongside lower SHBG and inflammatory markers, which makes a small free-testosterone bump biologically plausible without proving a durable testosterone-boosting effect.
edges.summary: Human evidence for boron as a free-testosterone booster is thin and internally inconsistent. One very small acute-to-short-term study reported an increase in free testosterone, while the better-known placebo-controlled bodybuilding trial found no meaningful hormonal benefit, so this remains a noisy supplement claim rather than a dependable endocrine strategy.
edges.caveats: The direct human literature is extremely sparse, underpowered, and old. The most positive signal comes from eight volunteers studied over only a week, which is not enough to justify confident marketing claims or broad hormonal-optimization advice.

evidence.citation: Naghii MR et al 2011 J Trace Elem Med Biol
evidence.notes: Comparative effects of daily and weekly boron supplementation on plasma steroid hormones and proinflammatory cytokines.
